panels.description:
Answers: how many jobs exist in the platform right now across all statuses?

Point-in-time snapshot from the polling query. Each value reflects the state of the jobs collection at the last poll interval.

- Rising: jobs are being created faster than they are completing or being cleaned up
- Stable: job creation and completion are balanced
- Falling: the platform is draining its backlog or jobs are being pruned
panels.title: Total Jobs

panels.description:
Answers: how many jobs have successfully completed?

Point-in-time snapshot from the polling query.

- High relative to Total Jobs: the platform has a healthy completion rate
- Low relative to Total Jobs: many jobs are still in-flight or have not finished successfully
panels.title: Complete Jobs

panels.description:
Answers: how many jobs are currently in 'canceled' status?

Point-in-time snapshot from the polling query.

- Near zero: normal operating state
- Elevated: users or automation are canceling jobs — may indicate upstream issues or deliberate intervention
panels.title: Canceled Jobs

panels.description:
Answers: how many jobs are currently in 'error' status?

Point-in-time snapshot from the polling query.

- Near zero: normal operating state
- Elevated: jobs are failing — review in combination with Job Error Rate % for severity context
panels.title: Error Jobs

panels.description:
Answers: are jobs starting, completing, and erroring at a consistent rate over time?

Shows new job starts, completions, and errors within each 30s window, sourced from the change stream counters.

- Start and complete lines tracking closely: healthy throughput balance
- Start line consistently above complete line: jobs are arriving faster than they finish — in-flight count is growing
- Error line rising: jobs are failing at an elevated rate — investigate immediately
- All lines flat: no job activity in the window
panels.title: Job Status Over Time

panels.description:
Answers: what percentage of all jobs in the collection have completed successfully?

Computed as complete / total from the current polling snapshot. This is a cumulative ratio, not a windowed rate — it reflects the platform's historical success rate.

- 95% or above: healthy
- 80–95%: elevated failure or cancellation — worth investigating
- Below 80%: significant job failures — immediate attention required
panels.title: Job Success Rate %

panels.description:
Answers: what percentage of all jobs in the collection have errored?

Computed as error / total from the current polling snapshot. Cumulative ratio.

- Below 1%: normal operating state
- 1–5%: elevated error rate — monitor closely
- Above 5%: critical error rate — investigate immediately
panels.title: Job Error Rate %

panels.description:
Answers: how many tasks exist in the platform right now across all statuses?

Point-in-time snapshot from the polling query. Each job typically spawns multiple tasks.

- Rising: task creation is outpacing completion and cleanup
- Stable: throughput is balanced
- Falling: the platform is draining its task backlog
panels.title: Total Tasks

panels.description:
Answers: how many tasks have successfully completed?

Point-in-time snapshot from the polling query.

- High relative to Total Tasks: most work has been processed successfully
- Low relative to Total Tasks: many tasks are still in-flight or have not completed
panels.title: Completed Tasks

panels.description:
Answers: how many tasks are actively being executed right now?

Point-in-time snapshot from the polling query.

- Stable value: the platform is processing work at a consistent pace
- Sustained spike: tasks are taking longer than expected — may indicate a bottleneck
- Near zero: the platform is idle or between job runs
panels.title: Running Tasks

panels.description:
Answers: how many tasks are currently in 'error' status?

Point-in-time snapshot from the polling query.

- Near zero: normal operating state
- Elevated: tasks are failing — check Task Error Rate by Server for per-node breakdown
panels.title: Errored Tasks

panels.description:
Answers: how many tasks are currently in 'canceled' status?

Point-in-time snapshot from the polling query. Cancellations are typically triggered by a parent job being canceled, not by task-level failures.

- Near zero: normal operating state
- Elevated: one or more parent jobs were likely canceled
panels.title: Canceled Tasks

panels.description:
Answers: how many tasks per second is each IAP node completing right now?

Average completion rate per node over the lookback window. Use this to identify which nodes are carrying the most load and whether throughput is consistent across the cluster.

- All nodes near equal: workload is well distributed
- One node significantly higher: that node is carrying a disproportionate share — may be intentional or indicate imbalance
- All nodes near zero: the platform is idle or the change stream is not receiving events
panels.title: Task Throughput Per Server

panels.description:
Answers: what is the overall platform task completion rate right now?

Sum of completion rates across all nodes. Use as a platform-wide health indicator.

- Rising: the platform is processing more work
- Stable: consistent throughput
- Falling or near zero: throughput has dropped — check individual nodes for failures or idle state
panels.title: Total Task Throughput

panels.description:
Answers: how many new tasks are being dispatched to each IAP node within each time window?

Task inserts detected by the change stream, broken out per node with a platform total. This reflects work being handed to the platform, not work being completed.

- Spikes on a single node: work is being directed unevenly
- Coordinated spikes across all nodes: a large job batch was triggered
- Total line flat: no new tasks are being created — platform may be idle
- A node absent from the chart: that node is not receiving work
panels.title: Net New started tasks

panels.description:
Answers: how is task completion throughput distributed across IAP nodes over time?

Rate of task completions per node (tasks/sec). Useful for identifying long-term workload imbalances.

- Lines tracking closely together: workload is evenly distributed
- One node consistently higher: that node is processing more tasks than others
- A node dropping to zero: that node may have stopped processing — investigate
panels.title: Task Completion Rate by Server Over Time

panels.description:
Answers: how has the number of actively running tasks changed over time?

Polling snapshot of tasks in 'running' status graphed over time. Updates on each poll interval, not in real time.

- Stable plateau: consistent processing rate
- Sustained climb: tasks are accumulating faster than they complete — potential bottleneck
- Sharp drop to zero: all tasks completed or the platform went idle
- Sawtooth pattern: normal batch behavior — tasks dispatched and drained in cycles
panels.title: Running Tasks Over Time

panels.description:
Answers: which IAP nodes have processed the most tasks since the exporter last restarted?

Cumulative share of task completions per node. Because this uses a counter, slices represent all-time totals since the last restart, not current activity.

- Equal slices: workload has been evenly distributed over time
- One dominant slice: that node has processed significantly more tasks — may be intentional or indicate imbalance
- A node absent: that node has not completed any tasks since the last restart
panels.title: Cumulative Task Completions by Server

panels.description:
Tracks the difference between task start and task completion rates (tasks/sec) over a 5-minute window, per IAP node. A value near zero indicates healthy throughput. A sustained positive value means tasks are starting faster than they are completing, which may signal a processing backlog.

- Positive value: tasks are starting faster than completing — backlog is growing
- Near zero: task throughput is balanced — healthy steady state
- Negative value: Tasks are completing faster than starting — backlog is draining (or the system is idle)
panels.title: Task Start/Complete Delta Rate

panels.description:
Answers: which IAP nodes are generating task errors, and at what rate?

Rate of new task errors per node (errors/sec), sourced from the change stream counter.

- All lines near zero: normal operating state
- One node elevated: that node is encountering failures — investigate its logs
- All nodes elevated simultaneously: a systemic issue is causing errors across the cluster
- Sustained rise on any node: errors are not self-resolving — intervention required
panels.title: Task Error Rate by Server

panels.description:
Answers: is each IAP node completing tasks as fast as they are being assigned?

Plots start rate and completion rate per node on the same axis. Each node has two lines — one for starts, one for completions.

- Start and complete lines close together: that node is keeping pace with its workload
- Start line consistently above complete line: tasks are queuing up on that node — a backlog is forming
- Complete line above start line: that node is draining a backlog or going idle
- All lines near zero: the platform is idle
panels.title: Task Start vs. Task Complete

panels.description:
Answers: which IAP nodes are seeing task cancellations, and how frequently?

Number of task cancellations per node within each lookback window. Cancellations are typically triggered by a parent job being canceled, not task-level failures.

- Near zero on all nodes: normal operating state
- Spike on a single node: a job running on that node was canceled
- Spike across all nodes simultaneously: a large batch job or workflow was canceled platform-wide
panels.title: Task Cancellations by Server

panels.description:
Answers: how do task start and completion rates compare per node over time?

Plots start rate and completion rate per node (tasks/sec). Unlike the delta panel, this shows raw rates rather than the difference, making it easier to see absolute throughput levels.

- Start and complete lines tracking together: healthy throughput
- Completion rate consistently below start rate: work is accumulating on that node
- Both rates declining together: platform throughput is dropping — may be expected (end of batch) or unexpected
- A node's lines both near zero: that node is idle or not receiving events
panels.title: Task Throughput (tasks/sec, 5m avg)
